name: Piano: chords, scales and the circle of fifths
description: Learn piano chords and scales key by key, walking the circle of fifths: major and minor triads, their inversions, suspended, diminished and augmented triads, seventh chords in every inversion, then major, minor, pentatonic and blues scales, plus an interactive circle of fifths to explore, quiz and race against the clock. Each card shows a chord or scale and you play it on a two-octave keyboard; inversions require the right bass note and scales are played in order. Made by Stefano Zucchini (github.com/Stefz29), shared under AGPL-3.0.
author: Stefano Zucchini

content.name: Piano: chords, scales and the circle of fifths
content.description: Learn piano chords and scales key by key, walking the circle of fifths: major and minor triads, their inversions, suspended, diminished and augmented triads, seventh chords in every inversion, then major, minor, pentatonic and blues scales, plus an interactive circle of fifths to explore, quiz and race against the clock. Each card shows a chord or scale and you play it on a two-octave keyboard; inversions require the right bass note and scales are played in order.

decks.name: Piano
decks.description: Chords on the keyboard, one key at a time round the circle of fifths: C G D A E B F♯ D♭ A♭ E♭ B♭ F.

decks.name: Piano::1 Triads
decks.description: Major and minor triads in root position and both inversions, then suspended, diminished and augmented triads.

decks.name: Piano::2 Seventh chords
decks.description: Major 7th, dominant 7th, minor 7th, half-diminished and diminished 7th chords in root position and every inversion.

decks.name: Piano::3 Scales
decks.description: Major, natural, harmonic and melodic minor, pentatonic and blues scales in every key, played tonic to tonic.

decks.name: Piano::4 Circle of fifths
decks.description: Explore the circle of fifths, then quiz yourself on keys, signatures, relative minors, chords and fifths.

decks.name: Piano::4 Circle of fifths::Memory run
decks.description: A timed run: place all twelve keys on an empty circle, once per practice day.

decks.name: Piano::5 Name the chord
decks.description: A chord lights up on the keyboard: name its root and quality, and with inversions its lowest note.

decks.name: Piano::6 Ear training
decks.description: A chord is played with nothing on screen: tell major, minor and the rest apart by ear.

decks.name: Piano::7 Chords in a key
decks.description: Build the diatonic chords of a key from the Roman numerals: I IV V first, then all seven triads, the sevenths, and the minor keys.

decks.name: Piano::8 Progressions
decks.description: Play chord progressions from Roman numerals, chord by chord: I-IV-V-I, ii-V-I and I-V-vi-IV in every key, then the minor cadence i-iv-V-i.

decks.name: Piano::9 Key signatures
decks.description: Read a key signature on a treble or bass staff and name the major key and its relative minor, sharps and flats.

types.name: Circle of fifths
types.description: An interactive circle of fifths. Explore mode: tap a key to see its seven chords, key signature and scale. Quiz mode: each review asks a new question (fill the blank key, count sharps and flats, relative minors, the chords of a key, fifths above and below). Memory mode: a timed run placing all twelve keys on an empty circle.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Optional line shown above the circle (also the card's title in lists).

fields.name: mode
fields.description: explore | quiz | memory

fields.name: questions
fields.description: Quiz kinds to draw from each review: fill, signature-count, signature-key, relative-minor, relative-major, degree, fifth-above, fifth-below.

types.demo:
// The correct answer for this variant (explore has none).
return key.answer ?? null;

types.name: Piano chord
types.description: Play a chord on a two-octave piano. Leave the root empty for a new random root every review, or fix it (C, F#, Bb...). Pick an inversion to require a specific lowest note; with "any", every voicing counts. Graded by pitch classes.

fields.name: prompt
fields.default: Build this chord on the keyboard.
fields.description: Shown above the chord name (also the card's title in lists).

fields.name: qualities
fields.description: Chord qualities to draw from: maj, min, dim, aug, sus2, sus4, maj7, 7, m7, m7b5, dim7.

fields.name: root
fields.description: Optional fixed root: C, F#, Bb, Eb, Db... Empty draws a random common root. A fixed root is spelled exactly, with double flats or sharps where the chord needs them.

fields.name: inversion
fields.description: any (every voicing counts), root, 1st, 2nd or 3rd. Otherwise the lowest key pressed must be that chord tone, or the score is halved. 3rd needs a seventh chord.

types.name: Piano: hear the chord
types.description: A chord is played (nothing is shown until you answer) and you pick its quality by ear. The root is random each review. After grading you see the chord on a two-octave keyboard and can replay it and the one you picked, on the same root, to compare.

fields.name: prompt
fields.default: What kind of chord is this?
fields.description: Shown above the Play button (also the card's title in lists).

fields.name: qualities
fields.description: Chord qualities to draw from: maj, min, dim, aug, sus2, sus4, maj7, 7, m7, m7b5, dim7. Only these appear as answer buttons.

fields.name: style
fields.description: block (all notes together), arpeggio (low to high, notes ringing) or both (arpeggio, then the block).

fields.name: root
fields.description: Optional fixed root: C, F#, Bb, Eb, Db... Empty draws a random root from C G D A E B F# Db Ab Eb Bb F.

types.name: Piano: chord of a key
types.description: Build a diatonic chord of a key on a two-octave piano, e.g. "Build the vi chord of E♭ major". The chord name is not shown. Leave the key empty for a random one (major: the twelve keys round the circle of fifths; minor: their relative minors). Minor keys use natural minor, with the harmonic-minor V and vii° (raised 7th) as in common practice. Spelling follows the key, so F♯ major's vii° is E♯ G♯ B. Graded by pitch classes; any voicing counts.

fields.name: prompt
fields.default: Build this chord on the keyboard.
fields.description: Shown above the question (also the card's title in lists).

fields.name: key
fields.description: Optional tonic: C, F#, Eb... (for mode minor, the minor tonic, e.g. C# for C♯ minor). Empty draws a random key.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: major, or minor (natural minor, with the harmonic-minor V and vii°).

fields.name: degrees
fields.description: Roman numerals to ask, e.g. I, IV, V. Case and ° are ignored: the card shows the true quality (vi in major, VI in minor).

fields.name: sevenths
fields.description: Ask the diatonic seventh chords (Imaj7 ii7 iii7 IVmaj7 V7 vi7 viiø7 in major) instead of triads.

fields.name: prompt

fields.name: ask

types.name: Piano: name the chord
types.description: A chord lights up on a two-octave keyboard; name it by picking its root and quality. With inversions on, the lowest lit key may not be the root, so you also pick the bass note (a slash chord, or "root pos."). Leave the root empty for a random root each review.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Shown above the keyboard (also the card's title in lists).

fields.name: qualities
fields.description: Chord qualities to draw from: maj, min, dim, aug, sus2, sus4, maj7, 7, m7, m7b5, dim7. Only these appear as answer buttons.

fields.name: root
fields.description: Optional fixed root: C, F#, Bb, Eb, Db... Empty draws a random root from C G D A E B F# Db Ab Eb Bb F.

fields.name: inversions
fields.description: none (root position only), triads (root, 1st or 2nd inversion) or all (also 3rd inversion for seventh chords). With inversions on, you also name the bass note.

types.demo: return { root: key.root, quality: key.quality, bass: key.bass };

types.name: Piano: chord progression
types.description: Play a chord progression in a key from its Roman numerals, chord by chord on a two-octave piano, e.g. "Play I-V-vi-IV in D♭ major". The chord names are not shown: work them out from the numerals. Leave the key empty for a random one (major: the twelve keys round the circle of fifths; minor: their relative minors, with the harmonic-minor V and vii°). Spelling follows the key. Each step is graded by pitch classes, any voicing or inversion counts, and the score is the mean of the steps.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Shown above the question (also the card's title in lists).

fields.name: key
fields.description: Optional tonic: C, F#, Eb... (for mode minor, the minor tonic). Empty draws a random key.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: major, or minor (natural minor, with the harmonic-minor V and vii°).

fields.name: progression
fields.description: Roman numerals separated by - or –, e.g. ii-V-I or I-V-vi-IV. Add 7 or maj7 for seventh chords: ii7-V7-Imaj7. Case is ignored: the card shows the true quality.

types.name: Piano scale
types.description: Play a scale on a two-octave piano, tonic to the tonic an octave higher, in order. Each review draws one of the scale ids. Graded note by note on pitch classes, so any starting octave and any octave jumps are fine; the result spells the scale for the key and plays it back.

fields.name: prompt
fields.default: Play this scale on the keyboard.
fields.description: Shown above the scale name (also the card's title in lists).

fields.name: root
fields.description: The tonic: C, F#, Bb, Eb, Db... Spelled exactly for the key, with double sharps or flats where the scale needs them.

fields.name: scales
fields.description: Scale ids to draw from each review: major, natural-minor, harmonic-minor, melodic-minor-asc, melodic-minor-desc, major-pentatonic, minor-pentatonic, major-blues, minor-blues. melodic-minor-desc is the natural minor played downwards from the upper tonic.

types.demo:
// The correct sequence as MIDI: from the lower tonic up, or from the upper tonic down.
return key.seq.map((t) => t.m);
